title: Soft evacuation: traffic fencing and capacity fallback policy
creator: Nadia Park
description: Implement a multi-region routing policy that performs graceful traffic evacuation from degraded regions using soft fencing (gradual ejection), capacity-aware fallback into compatible regions, and a soft circuit-backpressure layer to limit emergency amplification. This ticket covers policy definition, runtime gating hooks, metric-driven thresholds, rollout plan, and observability to validate SLO preservation during evacuations.
success_criteria: Evacuation policy can shift >95% of new requests away from a degraded zone within 30s under simulated outage without exceeding target p95 latency in fallback regions
No more than 10% increase in token cost for steady-state traffic during normal operation
Automated circuit backpressure prevents overload of fallback regions: fallback region CPU/GPU utilization stays <= 85% during failover tests
Playbook and runbook verified by SRE and Production ML team
design_notes: Policy consists of three layers: polite fencing (gradual reroute based on latency/errored requests), steered fallback (capacity-aware reweighting to compatible regions/models), and soft circuit backpressure (per-region rate limits and shedding thresholds)
Fencing uses exponential backoff on pinning score: small % of new sessions are re-pinned each evaluation window to avoid mass cold starts
Fallback picks region/model by compatibility matrix (model family, quantization variant). If exact variant not available, routers will prefer lower-cost variant with auto-quality-monitoring enabled
Circuit backpressure emits a telemetry token indicating degraded mode so downstream consoles can surface exact reason for shed requests
We will re-use existing routing API hooks (region-hint, capacity-hint) and add a new policy layer config: soft_eviction:{window_ms, step_pct, max_pct, backoff_factor}
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on internal staging region for 48h
Ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% for non-critical tenants with monitoring gates
Global enable: after 2 sustained canaries and signoff from SRE & ML quality
Emergency off-ramp: disable flag + immediate revert to last-stable routing weights
telemetry: per-region p50/p95/p99 latency (generation and total request path)
error rate (% 5xx and model mismatch errors)
fallback traffic fraction by region and model variant
region utilization (GPU mem, GPU util, CPU), queued request counts
eviction events and step changes (histogram of step_pct applied)
test_plan: Simulate progressive region degradation in chaos cluster: packet loss, increased tail latency, partial GPU OOMs
Run mix of interactive chat and embeddings workloads to validate variant selection and model fallbacks
Load test fallback regions to confirm soft circuit backpressure keeps utilization <=85%
Golden path regression: ensure no change to steady-state routing when feature flag disabled
Integration tests for routing config serialization and backwards compatibility with Dedicated customers
open_questions: Should prioritized enterprise customers be exempt from soft evacuation by default? (security vs reliability tradeoff)
What is the acceptable cold-start budget when re-pinning sessions (tokens and latency)?
How do we version quality evaluation for automatic variant downgrade to avoid silent regressions?
Do we surface evacuation reason to customers or only to internal dashboards?
Exact threshold tuning for circuit-open (utilization vs latency signals) requires empirical runs
